================================================================
PINNED OBJECTIVE
Extract what 10 successful traders collectively know, then build
ONE executable NQ strategy that preserves their ideas.

TRADINGVIEW v1 — IMPLEMENTATION MAP, PARITY KIT, AND VERDICT
Package contents: ORB_S5b_v1.pine (source), this document,
parity_reference_orb_2016_2026.csv (2,295 expected trades with
signal/entry/exit timestamps and prices from the verified
engine), parity_reference_s5b_states_2016_2026.csv (2,705 days
of expected S5b state timestamps), parity_check.py (automated
trade-list diff), S5b 12-day spot-check list (Section 6).
Nothing in the Pine reinterprets a rule. No optimization.
================================================================

1. PLAIN-ENGLISH IMPLEMENTATION MAP

Chart: 5-minute, NQ1! (or MNQ1!), timezone-independent — every
rule is computed on the America/New_York clock inside the
script.

MODULE A (the only thing that trades):
- 09:30–09:44:59 NY builds the 15-min opening range from the
  three 5m bars opening 09:30/09:35/09:40.
- From 09:45 through the 10:30 bar inclusive, the FIRST 5m bar
  that CLOSES beyond the OR with body ≥ 50% of its range sets
  the direction. First qualified direction wins; one trade/day.
- Entry: next 5m bar open (Pine's native next-bar market fill —
  process_orders_on_close is OFF, so the order placed at signal
  close fills at the next open, exactly like the research
  engine).
- Stop: opposite OR extreme, submitted as the ONLY intrabar
  order. Because it is the only intrabar order, TradingView's
  intrabar path assumptions cannot differ from the research
  engine's 1m touch logic — a bar either crosses the stop or it
  doesn't.
- Impossible-fill guard: if the fill lands beyond the stop
  (gap), the position is voided at once and tagged VOID_GAP —
  never booked as a win. (In 2,295 research trades this never
  occurred on 5m NQ; the guard exists for honesty.)
- Exit: the bar opening 15:55 closes the position AT ITS CLOSE
  (strategy.close immediately=true) = 16:00 NY, which equals
  the research engine's 15:59 1m close price.

MODULE B (classifier — zero orders):
- Opening balance = first six 5m bars (09:30–09:59).
- From the 10:00 bar: first CLOSE beyond OBH/OBL latches
  direction. Leg tracked exactly as researched (session-running
  extreme on the with side; anchor frozen at latch on the other).
- Pullback band 25–75% of the leg; >100% retrace = INVALIDATED
  (display state only — Round 3 proved this event is already
  owned by the ORB stop; v1 takes NO action on it).
- Failure = two consecutive bars with no new pullback progress
  (1-pt tolerance). Reassertion = close through prior bar's
  extreme, directional body, volume ≥ 1.2 × the WITHIN-DAY
  rolling 12-bar average (min 6 observations — computed from an
  intraday array, NOT ta.sma, which would leak across sessions).
- The ≥5-pt risk floor is checked at the NEXT bar's open, so the
  CONFIRMED timestamp in Pine equals the research engine's
  confirmation timestamp (which is also next-bar).
- No new state progress after the 11:30 bar (a confirmation
  signaled on the 11:30 bar may finalize at 11:35, matching the
  engine).

MODULE C: ALIGNED / DISAGREEMENT / UNRESOLVED, computed only
after both states exist. S5b never touches the ORB entry —
enforced structurally: Module A executes without reading any
Module B variable.

2. STATE MACHINE (text table)

 state  name                      entered when                      exits to
 0      WAITING                   session start                     1 (latch), stays 0
 1      DIRECTION LATCHED         first 5m close beyond OBH/OBL     2, -9
 2      PULLBACK ACTIVE           retrace 25–75% of leg             3, -9
 3      COUNTERATTACK FAILING     2-bar no-progress inside band     4*, -9
 4      S5b CONFIRMED             reassertion close + volume,       terminal (day)
                                  finalized next open if risk ≥5
 -9     INVALIDATED               retrace > 100% of leg             terminal (day)
 (*state 3→4 may take multiple attempts; a failed risk floor
  returns to scanning, exactly like the engine)

3. ALERT / EVENT SPECIFICATION
Events (alert() JSON, once per bar close):
 ORB_LONG_ENTRY / ORB_SHORT_ENTRY  — at signal close; entry
   executes next open, payload carries signal close + stop
 S5B_LONG_CONFIRMED / S5B_SHORT_CONFIRMED — at finalize bar
 ORB_STOP — bar on which the stop was crossed
 SESSION_CLOSE_EXIT — 15:55 bar
Payload fields: ver, sym, ts (NY), event, dir, entry, stop, orH,
orL, s5state, s5dir, align, id (sym_yyyymmdd_event). Simple
alertcondition() hooks are also exposed for the 4 entry/confirm
events. No credentials anywhere in Pine; automation consumes the
JSON via webhook when we get to paper wiring.

4. TRADINGVIEW SETUP
1. Chart: CME_MINI:NQ1!, 5-minute. Chart timezone irrelevant.
2. IMPORTANT — data settings: continuous contract NQ1! defaults
   to UNADJUSTED. For price-level parity vs the research
   (back-adjusted) either enable "Adjust for contract changes"
   in symbol settings, or accept that historical PRICES differ
   by the roll offset while DATES/TIMES/DIRECTIONS still match
   (intraday-relative rules are offset-invariant within a day).
3. Extended or regular hours both work — the script gates
   everything by NY clock. RTH chart recommended (cleaner).
4. Add strategy → Strategy Tester → Export "List of Trades" CSV
   for the parity run.
5. Alerts: create one alert on the strategy, "Any alert()
   function call", webhook optional for paper automation later.

5. ORB PARITY — PROCEDURE AND EXPECTED RESULT
This chat cannot execute Pine; parity is a one-export job on
your side, and the reference plus the checker are in this
package so either AI can grade it mechanically.

a) Export the TradingView List of Trades CSV (as deep as your
   plan's 5m history goes — note TV intraday history is limited;
   expect roughly 2011+ at best, and treat whatever window TV
   serves as the parity window).
b) Run: python parity_check.py <tv_export.csv>
   It matches by date against
   parity_reference_orb_2016_2026.csv and buckets every
   mismatch: MISSING_DAY / EXTRA_DAY / DIRECTION / ENTRY_TIME /
   ENTRY_PRICE / STOP / EXIT_TIME / EXIT_PRICE, with tolerance
   inputs for the price-offset case (unadjusted feed).
c) Anchors for a 60-second eyeball before the full run — the
   reference's bookends: first trade 2016-01-04 and the totals
   2,295 trades / 216-227 per full year (per-year counts are in
   the reference CSV).
Accept nothing short of trade-list parity on days where TV data
exists; category-coded mismatches come back to me and I resolve
them — the strategy itself does not change.

6. S5b SPOT-CHECK — 12 PREREGISTERED DAYS
Load each day on the chart and compare the on-chart state labels
to the engine's expected timestamps (all NY, 5m bar opens;
CONFIRMED timestamp = finalize bar):
 CONFIRMED    2016-01-13  latch 10:10 ▼  confirm 10:35  (entry 7070.50 / stop 7102.50)
 CONFIRMED    2018-06-18  latch 10:20 ▲  confirm 10:40  (9953.25 / 9929.50)
 CONFIRMED    2022-07-22  latch 10:05 ▼  confirm 11:25  (15083.50 / 15205.50)
 CONFIRMED    2026-06-16  latch 10:15 ▼  confirm 10:25  (30713.00 / 30891.00)
 INVALIDATED  2016-01-25  latch 10:00 ▲  invalid 11:10
 INVALIDATED  2021-03-30  latch 10:15 ▼  invalid 11:30
 INVALIDATED  2026-06-22  latch 10:05 ▲  invalid 10:25
 LATCH-ONLY   2016-02-11  latch 11:30 ▼   (never enters band)
 LATCH-ONLY   2021-03-16  latch 10:00 ▲
 LATCH-ONLY   2026-06-15  latch 11:00 ▲
 NO-LATCH     2016-01-15  (no 5m close beyond OB through 11:30)
 NO-LATCH     2026-06-25  (same)
Prices are back-adjusted research values — on an unadjusted
feed, expect the same TIMESTAMPS with offset prices except on
the current contract (2026 rows), where prices should match to
the tick. The full 2,705-day state reference is in the CSV for
deeper sampling. The volume-dependent CONFIRMED rows are the
ones most at risk from feed differences (Section 7, item 4).

7. UNAVOIDABLE TV-vs-FIRSTRATE DISCREPANCIES (known in advance)
1) Back-adjustment: TV continuous defaults unadjusted; research
   is adjusted. Dates/times/directions invariant intraday;
   historical price levels differ by the roll offset.
2) Intraday history depth: TV 5m history is plan-limited and
   far shorter than 2008; the parity window is whatever TV
   serves, and the 2016–2026 reference covers the realistic
   maximum.
3) Session template: TV's futures RTH runs to 16:15 NY; the
   research day ends 16:00. The script clock-gates to
   09:30–16:00, so the 16:00–16:15 tail is ignored (flat by
   then). Exit price = 16:00 close = research 15:59 1m close.
4) VOLUME FEED — the one that matters: TV's futures volume can
   differ from FirstRate's. ORB parity is immune (no volume
   rule). S5b CONFIRMED is volume-gated (1.2× within-day
   average), so borderline confirmations can flip on a
   different feed. This is why the spot-check includes four
   CONFIRMED days; if those four match, the classifier is
   feed-robust enough for display/alert duty.
5) Half-days: the research excluded sessions with <200 1m bars;
   Pine trades any day with a complete OR. Expect a handful of
   holiday-eve count differences — the checker buckets them as
   MISSING/EXTRA days.
6) Roll dates: TV's roll convention may differ from FirstRate's
   by a day; intraday logic is unaffected, but the specific
   contract quoted on a roll day can shift OR levels slightly
   vs the research series.

8. PAPER-AUTOMATION READINESS — RECOMMENDATION
CONDITIONAL YES. The implementation is faithful, order-complete,
and alert-instrumented, and nothing in it can retroactively
filter the ORB entry. But per your own rule — do not accept
approximate similarity — it is NOT signed off until the two
gates on your side run: (1) the ORB List-of-Trades export
passes parity_check.py on the overlapping window with only
category-3/5/6-class discrepancies, and (2) the 12-day S5b
spot-check matches, especially the four CONFIRMED timestamps.
Pass both → wire the alert webhook to the paper executor and
start the forward ledger. Fail either → mismatches come back to
me by category and I fix the implementation, never the strategy.

WHAT v1 DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO (per the freeze): no add or
resize at S5b confirmation, no exit on disagreement, no NO-LATCH
action, no trailing, no VWAP/EMA/ATR, no prop rules, no live
money. Direction-agreement sizing stays PARKED as its own future
preregistered test.
================================================================
